newsitem.title: UK: PIA moves to tighten rules on pension opt-outs.
newsitem.headline: PIA moves to tighten rules on pension opt-outs.

text.p: Britain's Personal Investment Authority (PIA), which regulates the pension industry, on Monday put forward new proposals to tighten future transfers or opt-outs from occupational pension schemes.
Under the proposals all transactions related to pension transfers and opt-outs will have to be checked by a suitably qualified pensions expert.
In the past firms would have to demonstrate a certain business standard but there was no requirement to display particular expertise.
The consultative document follows moves to speed up compensation for victims of pension misselling by banks and insurance companies.

Only last week companies were given new deadlines to sort out the scandal in which as many as 1-1/2 million people may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions instead of staying in occupational schemes.

Labour's new Treasury minister Helen Liddell also called in senior executives from the 28 worst offending firms, leaving them in no doubt that the government wanted to see progress in sorting out compensation.
Liddell warned that unless it could be convinced of their sincerity, companies could face a stiffer regulatory regime under planned reform of the financial services industry.

"The PIA has already established minimum standards of knowledge and competence for advisers but considers additional requirements necessary for this type of business," said the PIA chairman's Joe Palmer.
Responses to the proposals are expected by the end of June.
